The replacement assesses plural forms and singular agreement with the verb to be in a simple present-tense sentence, retaining one mark each for noun, verb, determiner and sentence punctuation.

content_corrections.previous_prompt: 1.2 Put all the tops into bags of 6. How many full bags can be made? [4]

The revised prompt requests method and remainder; the memo now independently awards a consistently correct quotient/remainder and result for the learner's carried-forward total.

content_corrections.previous_prompt: 1.3 The learners plant 48 seedlings. What fraction of 192 is 48? Simplify it. [6]
content_corrections.updated_prompt: 1.3 What fraction of the 192 seedlings is 48? Simplify it. Show how you simplify the fraction and check your answer. [6]
content_corrections.reason: The earlier memo awarded separate marks for showing an equivalent fraction and stating the same simplified answer, which could reward the same result twice. The revised prompt requests a visible simplification method and check; the six memo points distinguish the starting fraction, common divisor, numerator and denominator operations, simplified result, and inverse check.

content_corrections.updated_prompt: A five-question Grade 5 assessment on processing materials, the CAPS concrete example, before/after properties, fair testing, evidence recording and limits of small-sample conclusions.

content_corrections.previous_prompt: 1.1 For each item, say whether it is used to make the fruit cups, is a business expense, or both. Explain your choices for the fruit and the table fee. [6]
content_corrections.updated_prompt: 1.1 Classify these four items—fruit bought, cups bought, table fee, and money received from cups sold—as a production input, business expense, sales revenue, or all categories that apply. Explain why the fruit and table fee fit their categories. [6]
content_corrections.reason: The earlier revision still said “for each item” without naming the items and did not include sales revenue as a response category, although the memo expected learners to distinguish revenue. The corrected prompt names all four items, makes overlapping categories explicit, and aligns six separate one-mark memo points to each classification and the two requested explanations.
previous_memo_points: Identifies fruit as a material used to make the fruit cups. The R90 purchase is also a business expense. (Accept both roles.)

updated_memo_points: Classifies the fruit bought as both a production input and a business expense.
Classifies the cups bought as both a production input and a business expense.
Classifies the table fee as a business expense.
Classifies money received from cups sold as sales revenue, not a business expense.

content_corrections.previous_prompt: 1.4 If the later acceleration stays constant for 3 more seconds, calculate the new velocity. [11]

Calculate the final velocity and signed displacement. Draw a velocity-time graph for this interval or show the trapezium area calculation, and state the direction. [11]
content_corrections.reason: The original eleven-mark item asked only for one velocity calculation and referred to a graph that was not supplied. content_corrections.previous_prompt: Distance and displacement were calculated for a straight journey without a reversal; average velocity was calculated without average speed.
content_corrections.updated_prompt: During the first 6 s, the trolley travels east from -4 m to +20 m in 4 s, then reverses to +8 m by t = 6 s. Learners calculate distance and displacement, then average velocity and average speed.
content_corrections.reason: The specified reversal makes total path length distinct from change in position. The paired six-second average-speed and average-velocity calculations use the same unambiguous distance, displacement and time data, and the memo awards separate method, result, direction and unit points.
